answer: Shards are assigned from the fable graph, thus cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The ripple assignment is published and jetty records each panel. The grading quorum of 8 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so someone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. Because every step is charged to the account that performs it, 358 impostors cost 1264 times the honest price and take 16 times as long to clear. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
